# Results — Study 288 (Ramadan-Effect) on a buyable MENA proxy

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Ramadan windows are
hardcoded in [`data.py`](../ramadan_effect/data.py) (Umm al-Qura calendar, 2000–2026).
The MENA proxy is the iShares MSCI Saudi Arabia ETF (`KSA`) and the placebo is the
S&P 500 (`^GSPC`), both monthly closes via yfinance, cached at
`_cache/ramadan_proxy.parquet`. Match the fingerprint below to confirm you hold the
same data. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| iShares MSCI Saudi Arabia (`KSA`, monthly, auto-adjusted) | 2015-10 → 2026-06 | 129 months (11 Ramadan) | `7dfeb747d94a` |
| S&P 500 (`^GSPC`, monthly) placebo | 2015-10 → 2026-06 | 129 months | (same panel) |
| Ramadan windows | Hijri 1420–1447 (2000–2026) | 28 windows | hardcoded constant |

Returns are price/total return as delivered by yfinance `auto_adjust=True`
(distributions reinvested for both series). A month is labelled **Ramadan** when
≥ 50% of its calendar days fall inside a Ramadan window — known years in advance,
so there is no look-ahead.

## The headline — a big-looking gap on tiny n

| Arm | n months | mean return | annualised | up-month rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Ramadan months | 11 | **+2.86%/mo** | **+40.2%/yr** | 72.7% |
| Rest of year | 118 | **+0.46%/mo** | **+5.7%/yr** | 55.1% |
| **Gap (Ramadan − rest)** | | **+239.3 bps/mo** | (~+34pp/yr) | +17.6pp |

The annualised numbers look spectacular (+40%/yr vs +6%/yr). The catch is the
sample: **11 Ramadan months** since the proxy began trading in 2015.

## Is the gap significant? — No

| Test | Statistic | Reading |
|---|--:|---|
| HAC (Newey-West, 3 lags) t on the Ramadan-dummy OLS slope | **+1.55** | below the |t| ≥ 2 bar |
| Welch t-test (Ramadan vs rest, unequal var) | **+1.51** (p = 0.156) | not significant |
| Label-permutation test (10,000 shuffles, two-sided \|gap\|) | **p = 0.150** | ~1-in-7 by chance |

The single-series HAC t on the Ramadan-month mean alone is +3.10 (i.e. Ramadan
months were reliably positive), but that is **not** the claim under test — the
claim is that Ramadan months *beat the rest*, and that difference (the dummy
slope) carries t = 1.55.

## The S&P 500 placebo — clean

| Arm | gap | HAC dummy t | permutation p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| S&P 500, Ramadan − rest | **−216.6 bps/mo** | **−1.53** | 0.119 |

A real behavioural Ramadan effect should be *absent* on a non-Muslim-majority
tape. It is: the S&P's Ramadan-month gap is **negative**, not positive. So the
MENA proxy's positive sign is at least region-specific and not a global
lunar-calendar artifact — the one fact that nudges the Signal from None to
**Weak**.

## The volatility claim (Bialkowski et al. H2) — marginal

| Arm | annualised vol |
|---|--:|
| Ramadan months | 17.3% |
| Rest of year | 18.3% |

Ramadan vol is *directionally* lower (consistent with "calmer months"), but the
1.0pp difference on 11 observations is not testable.

## The n = 11 problem

With ~5.3% monthly volatility, 11 Ramadan months and 118 others, the minimum
detectable mean difference at 80% power (two-sided, α = 0.05) is:

    MDE ≈ (t_crit + t_power) · σ · √(1/n_ram + 1/n_rest) ≈ 470 bps/mo

The observed gap (239 bps/mo) is only **51% of the detection floor**. Even if the
+2.4pp gap were structurally real, this sample cannot confirm it — the literature
sample (1989–2007, 14 local indices) had far more Ramadan-market observations.

## Could you trade it?

Strategy: long the MENA proxy only in Ramadan months, flat otherwise. One execution
lag is unnecessary (the calendar is known in advance), but each entry/exit pays a
round-trip cost (one-way 30 bps × NAV; a US-listed ETF long, no borrow).

| Leg | annualised |
|---|--:|
| Buy & hold the MENA proxy | **+6.5%/yr** |
| Ramadan-timing (gross) | +2.8%/yr |
| Ramadan-timing (net, 30 bps one-way) | **+2.2%/yr** |
| Cost drag | 61 bps/yr |

Sitting in cash 11 months a year forfeits most of the index's compounding; the
single-month edge — itself not significant — cannot make up the shortfall.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The Ramadan effect has genuine academic support (Bialkowski,
  Etebari & Wisniewski 2012) and the *right sign* on our buyable proxy (+239 bps/mo,
  Ramadan vol lower, placebo clean), but the difference is **not** statistically
  significant on the real tape: HAC dummy t = 1.55, Welch t = 1.51, perm p = 0.15
  on 11 Ramadan months. Literature support without a clean HAC t ≥ 2 on the real
  tape is, by the desk rubric, **Weak** — not Real. Survivorship/representativeness
  is named: `KSA` is a single coarse proxy starting in 2015, an upper bound.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No vehicle harvests the gross gap: a Ramadan-timing
  clock nets +2.2%/yr against +6.5%/yr buy-and-hold, dominated by simply holding
  the index, with ~60 bps/yr round-trip drag.
- **Mostly busted on the buyable tape.** The original 1989–2007 local-index effect
  may well be real; on a post-2015 US-listed proxy with n = 11 it is inside the
  noise band and the placebo is clean.
